messages:
maria: FYI getting alerts from monitoring: east3a p4d pool showing repeated GPU block-attach timeouts + IO latency spikes. Pod attach failures ~12% over last 10m.
ops-bot: [ALERT] east3a-gpu-pool: device-attach-timeout x12 in 10m, avg-attach-ms 2200, baseline 120.
andrew: Copy — can someone pull kernel/dmesg logs from one of the failing nodes? guessing NVMe flakiness or host-side attach race.
liam: I grabbed one: /var/log/kern.log shows repeated "blk_update_request: I/O error" during attach + "nvme0: timeout" at ~2000ms.
jess: Suggest soft-cordon the remaining healthy p4d nodes in east3a to avoid new pods landing there while we triage. Don't hard drain yet — keep existing workloads running where possible.
maria: Agreed. Plan proposal: 1) soft-cordon (taint + no new scheduling) east3a p4d nodes 2) increase autoscaler max for east3b/c p4d and p3 pools 3) shift inference LB weights away from east3a by 40% 4) fallback non-latency critical batch jobs to cpu-gpu-mix spot pools 5) keep canary traffic to 5% for verification.
liam: Commands I'm running now: ```kubectl label node ip-10-0-5-21 taint/redwood-maint=soft:NoSchedule && kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-5-21 redwood/soft-cordon=true``` Doing per-node so we don't cause mass reshuffles.
ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed: rolling-update policy for models/service-inference will respect node affinity; watch for increased queue length.
andrew: We'll want to bump warm caches in east3b before shifting too much traffic — KV cache warmup matters for latency. Nina, can you pre-warm embeddings cache for top N models?
nina: On it. Spawning warmers in east3b, targeting top 30 models (by 95th p99 requests). ETA ~8m.
jess: Also recommend temporarily disabling aggressive packing on the runtime in east3a to avoid IO amplification: set runtime.conf: batching.enabled=true but batching.max_size=8 -> lower pressure.
clarence: Cost note: if we spin up more on-demand p4d in east3b that's ~2.4x cost vs spot. We should prefer spot where possible but keep reserved for critical routes. Approve hybrid approach.
maria: For traffic shift: manual LB change now - move 40% weight from east3a to east3b, 20% to east3c, leave 40% for east3a to serve stateful sessions. We'll iterate after metrics.
andrew: I patched autoscaler: maxNodes east3b+p3 pool +6, east3c+p4d +4. Also set scale-up cooldown to shorter (60s) to react.
liam: Monitoring dashboards: node attach errors -> dropping after cordon? so far no new attaches on cordoned nodes. Existing failing pods still running but degraded.
nina: Warmers done. KV hit rate east3b up to 78% from 12% prewarm in 9m. Good.
jess: Running verification curl to a few canary endpoints through east3b: latency p50 ~22ms, p99 ~170ms (acceptable).
andrew: One concern: some stateful sessions pinned to east3a (persistent volumes). We should avoid forcing PV detach unless necessary. That means keep ~30-40% capacity in east3a for sticky sessions.
maria: Agreed. We'll avoid volume migrations unless node fails health checks. If attach failures escalate to >30% we escalate to cross-zone rebind.
ops-bot: [INFO] routing-change applied: east3a=40%, east3b=40%, east3c=20% by traffic-switcher v1.3.
clarence: Heads up finance: projected delta if we keep extra on-demand for 12h is ~$18k. If we can stabilize and move back to spots within 4h, estimate $5k.
liam: Action items: - keep soft-cordon on remaining east3a p4d nodes - monitor attach failures and io errors - scale up east3b/c as patched - prewarm caches (done) - maintain 5% canary
jess: I'll keep runtime config change for batching in place for 30m then re-evaluate.
andrew: If errors fall below 3% for 20m we can start draining the two worst nodes (safe drains) and run disk checks.
maria: Great. If we see any PV detach errors or replication lag we escalate to storage oncall. Otherwise I'll coordinate stakeholder update in 15m.
liam: small note — observed one pod restart due to OOM when moved to p3, might need to nudge memory request for that workload.
nina: logging shows model-cache miss for that pod, likely warmup gap. I'll bump memory request + warm that instance.
maria: Thanks all. I'll post an incident summary once we have stable metrics for 30m. :thumbsup:
